items: Hal-pazeer (solvable): algorithm ise mehdood waqt mein hal kar sakta hai, saaf inputs, outputs aur qadam ba qadam tareeqe ke saath. Misal: do integers ka greatest common divisor (GCD) Euclidean algorithm se.

Na-qabil-e-hal (unsolvable): koi algorithm ise har soorat mein hal nahi kar sakta. Misal: Halting Problem, yeh tay karna ke diya gaya program aakhir ruk jayega ya hamesha chalta rahega; Alan Turing ne saabit kiya ke koi aam algorithm har program aur input ke jore ke liye ise hal nahi kar sakta.

blocks.text: Euclidean algorithm jore (a, b) ko (b, a / b ki baqi) se badalta rehta hai jab tak baqi 0 na ho: GCD(48, 18): 48 = 2 x 18 + 12, 18 = 1 x 12 + 6, 12 = 2 x 6 + 0, to GCD 6 hai. Pecheeda masle par kaam se pehle jaanch lein ke woh hal-pazeer hai; is se waqt aur wasail bachte hain (Tip).

blocks.prompt: Na-qabil-e-hal masail ke baare mein kya sach hai (MCQ 3)?
blocks.explanation: (b) unhein koi algorithm hal nahi kar sakta.

blocks.prompt: Halting Problem na-qabil-e-hal kyun hai aur is ke asraat kya hain, samjhaiye (long question 2).
blocks.explanation: Farz karein program H hamesha bata sakta hai ke koi program kisi input par rukega ya nahi. Aisa program D banayein jo H se khud D ke baare mein pooche aur phir ulat kare: H kahe D rukega to D hamesha chalta rahe; H kahe D chalta rahega to D ruk jaye. H ka har jawab ghalat hota hai, to H maujood nahi ho sakta (Turing ki tazad wali daleel). Asraat: koi tool har program ke na-khatam loops nahi pakar sakta, programs ke kuch sawalon ka jawab kabhi khud-kaar tareeqe se nahi mil sakta, aur computers ki bunyadi hadein hain.

items: Hal-pazeer: algorithm mehdood waqt mein khatam (48 aur 18 ka GCD 6).
Na-qabil-e-hal: koi algorithm tamam inputs par nahi chalta (Halting Problem, Turing).
